name: Shecaniah
overview: Shecaniah was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Hananiah. His mention in Scripture is brief, with no additional notes expanding on his life or role. His identity is primarily grounded in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Shecaniah means 'Yahweh has taken up his abode,' reflecting a theophoric element that honors God’s presence. This name highlights a devotional aspect common in Hebrew names, though it was not given directly by God according to the record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Shecaniah as the son of Hananiah, and it is inferred that Shemaiah was his father. Beyond these relationships, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shecaniah’s significance lies in his genealogical mention, which situates him within the lineage of Judah. This genealogy helps to establish the continuity of God’s people and their tribal heritage, underscoring the faithfulness of God in preserving His covenant community. Although he does not have a prominent narrative role, his inclusion affirms the detailed record-keeping that supports the biblical story of God's unfolding plan.
